findings.claim: R7's timestamp+suffix scheme is presented as ensuring the three IDs differ at gate close, but its uniqueness-by-construction relies on a load-bearing unstated assumption: that ISO-8601 timestamps captured at dispatch time will not collide AND that the 4-hex suffix is sufficient entropy when timestamps DO tie. R7 also says 'collision can happen only via fixture / manual injection / closer-parser bug' — yet two near-simultaneously-dispatched forked sub-agents on the same wall-clock millisecond with independently-generated 4-hex suffixes have a 1/65,536 collision probability per dispatch pair, not zero. The PRD asserts collision is essentially impossible without naming the load-bearing assumption.
findings.evidence: R7 lines 80-87: 'writer-{ISO-8601-timestamp}-{4-hex-suffix}', 'xtr-{round}-{ISO-8601-timestamp}-{4-hex-suffix}', 'applier-{ISO-8601-timestamp}-{4-hex-suffix}'. Phrase 'best-effort consistency check' admits the gap implicitly but doesn't surface the assumption ('timestamps do not tie at sub-millisecond AND suffix entropy is independent across sub-agent dispatches'). AC-15's collision-detection unit fixture (lines 301-315) tests the closer's PARSING of an injected collision but does not test whether real dispatch can produce one — so the doc-level claim that collision needs 'fixture / manual injection / closer-parser bug' is asserted, not engineered.
findings.proposed_change: ADD an explicit assumption statement under R7 in the form: 'ASSUMPTION: timestamp+suffix uniqueness is best-effort by construction; the design assumes (a) ISO-8601 timestamps with millisecond precision rarely tie across forked-sub-agent dispatches that are by definition staggered, and (b) the independently-generated 4-hex suffix provides ~16-bit collision avoidance when (a) fails. 027 will replace this with runtime-introspected IDs that are unique by construction.' AND add a sentence to R7's closing paragraph explicitly framing collision as 'rare-but-non-zero under real dispatch, not impossible' — this is the chain-don't-absorb honest framing per the goal-level Non-goal.
findings.lens: What unstated assumption is load-bearing in this artefact?

findings.claim: R3's three-round mini-debate assumes the cross-task reviewer can ALWAYS sharpen with new evidence at Round 3 — but the cross-task reviewer's two lenses (coherence + better-arrangement) operate on the WHOLE task list as a single artefact. Once the applier has applied accepted findings AND rejected others with rationale, the cross-task reviewer's 'new evidence' surface is structurally narrower than the per-task case: the artefact has changed only in the ways the applier accepted, and rejections are usually rejected because the applier disagrees with the LENS-application, not because new evidence will emerge. The PRD doesn't state whether 'always has new evidence' is a load-bearing assumption (justifying R3's symmetry with per-task three-round debate) or just convergence-discipline-by-default (in which case the third round may often be a no-op).
findings.evidence: R3 lines 60-66 mandates four sub-steps including E.4.5.3 sharpen + E.4.5.4 applier final pass. Interview Round 3 ('three rounds so a decision has to be made after three') and Round 7 ('full three-round flow with the applier playing the orchestrator's role') name the convergence discipline but neither states what 'sharpening' looks like at the whole-set lens. The role-def file (R1) defers lens-checklist sub-questions, so there's no upstream artefact specifying what new whole-set evidence emerges between R1 and R3. The mini-debate symmetry with per-task R1/R2/R3 is argued by analogy (Round 3 'so the existing Gate 3 convergence rules apply'), not by load-bearing whole-set-lens analysis.
findings.proposed_change: ADD a clause under R3 stating: 'ASSUMPTION (under test by R11 fixture): the cross-task reviewer's R3 sharpen surface — re-reading the post-applier tasks.md + applier rationale — yields meaningfully new evidence in non-trivial cases. If the R11 worked-example fixture demonstrates that R3 routinely produces empty findings, the three-round contract should be revisited in 027 (downgrade to two-round + escalate-on-rejection).' AND add to R11's fixture-content requirements: 'the fixture's R3 sharpen MUST produce non-empty new evidence (not merely re-asserted severity) so the assumption is binary-falsifiable.'
findings.lens: What unstated assumption is load-bearing in this artefact?

findings.anchor: R5 (Phase F invocation reading existing tasks.md without re-running A-D)
findings.claim: R5 says Phase F 'skips Phases A / B / C / D entirely' and takes three inputs including the post-Round-2 tasks.md. The unstated assumption is that the re-invoked `specflow:task --apply-cross-task-feedback {NNN-slug}` can read the existing tasks.md and operate on it WITHOUT the artefact-chain verification that A.1/A.2/A.3 normally do — i.e. the applier trusts the parent invocation's chain verification. R15 strengthens this ('the chain is already verified by the parent Gate 3 invocation that triggered the applier') but still presents it as a one-line statement, not a load-bearing assumption that cross-cuts the resume-logic in Phase A. If a user manually invokes `specflow:task --apply-cross-task-feedback` on a feature whose tasks.md is corrupted or whose PRD has been edited mid-Gate-3, the applier silently skips chain verification.
findings.evidence: R5 lines 71-74: 'When invoked this way, `specflow:task` skips Phases A / B / C / D entirely and enters a new Phase F'. R15 lines 119-122: 'when invoked with `--apply-cross-task-feedback`, the skill jumps to Phase F directly without re-running Phase A's verify-the-artefact-chain step (the chain is already verified by the parent Gate 3 invocation that triggered the applier).' The assumption 'parent Gate 3 invocation triggered the applier' is load-bearing — but the PRD does not state what happens when the applier is invoked manually (e.g. a user re-running it after a partial Phase F failure).
findings.proposed_change: ADD to R15: 'ASSUMPTION: `--apply-cross-task-feedback` is invoked exclusively from a Phase E.4.5.2 / E.4.5.4 dispatch in the parent Gate 3 run. Manual invocation by the user is a non-supported entry point in v2.5; the Phase A skip is justified ONLY because the parent run guarantees chain verification.' AND add a Phase A guard: 'If `--apply-cross-task-feedback` is invoked AND no in-flight Gate 3 manifest is detected (the parent run did not write the dispatch handoff), the applier MUST still run A.1's chain-verify step before entering Phase F.' This makes the load-bearing assumption explicit AND adds the fallback that respects it.

findings.claim: R2's threshold of '<3 tasks skips, 3+ runs' is asserted as mechanical convention but the load-bearing tradeoff is unstated. Interview Round 11 confirms 'real-world calibration: had a project with only 3 tasks; coherence/arrangement just barely meaningful at that count' — i.e. 3 is the floor, not the optimum. The PRD doesn't surface the tradeoff: a feature with EXACTLY 3 tasks where all relationships are obvious-by-inspection (e.g. T1 setup → T2 implement → T3 test) gets cross-task review with high latency and likely no findings, while a 2-task feature with subtle coherence concerns gets nothing. The threshold is a heuristic, not a meaningful-by-construction floor.
findings.evidence: R2 lines 56-58: 'When fewer than 3 tasks exist, Phase E.4.5 is skipped entirely.' Interview Round 11 lines 94-97: 'real-world calibration ... very small but coherence/arrangement just barely meaningful at that count.' The PRD frames the threshold as Simplicity-First-justified but doesn't discuss the asymmetric error mode (false-negative on 2-task features with subtle coherence issues vs false-positive on 3-task linear-flow features).
findings.proposed_change: ADD to R2 a Tradeoff sub-clause: 'TRADEOFF: the threshold accepts a false-negative on 2-task features whose coherence might benefit from review (e.g. one task sub-summing the other) AND a false-positive on 3-task features whose flow is obvious-by-inspection (e.g. setup → implement → test). The latency cost of the 3-task false-positive is bounded by R2.5's three-round mini-debate length; the false-negative is bounded by per-task review still firing. Per the Non-goal, this is mechanical not configurable; revisit if the worked-example fixture shows the false-positive rate exceeds 50% on 3-task linear-flow features.'
findings.lens: What unstated assumption is load-bearing in this artefact?

findings.anchor: R10 (per-task Round 3 sharpen against post-cross-task tasks.md)
findings.claim: R10's per-task Round 3 sharpen sees the post-cross-task tasks.md (different from the post-Round-2 tasks.md per-task reviewers saw at Round 1). The load-bearing assumption is that per-task reviewers' lenses can MEANINGFULLY re-evaluate against an artefact they didn't see at R1 — i.e. their R1 findings remain valid lenses to apply to a transformed artefact. But if the cross-task applier merged T3+T7, the Goal-Driven Reviewer's R1 finding on T3's coverage no longer maps to a stable T-id; the per-task reviewer's R3 sharpen surface is structurally ambiguous (does T3's R1 finding apply to the merged task, the dropped one, or neither?). R10 says 'this catches per-task issues the cross-task revisions may have introduced' but doesn't state whether per-task reviewers re-fire fresh against the new artefact OR sharpen-vs-R1 with a new artefact baseline.
findings.evidence: R10 lines 99-104: 'Per-task reviewers re-fire against the post-applier `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` — i.e. they see the cross-task-applied changes as the artefact they're sharpening on.' This conflates 're-fire' (fresh R1-like pass on the new artefact) with 'sharpen' (R3 pass referencing R1+R2). The Codex pre-gate finding [MAJOR] E added the B.4 re-run guarantee but the per-task R3 lens question is unaddressed: if T3 has been merged out of existence, what does the Surgical Reviewer's Round 1 finding on T3 'sharpen' to?
findings.proposed_change: ADD a clause to R10: 'CLARIFICATION: Phase E.5 per-task reviewers operate as a hybrid R3 — they sharpen R1 findings whose anchored T-id still exists in the post-applier tasks.md (standard R3 sharpen surface) AND treat R1 findings whose T-id was merged-out / dropped as auto-resolved (record in manifest as `resolved-by-cross-task-merge: T{N}->T{M}` or `resolved-by-cross-task-drop`). Net-new findings on tasks introduced by the applier (e.g. a merged T3+T7 → new T3.5) are recorded as `round-3-net-new` per-task findings AND require their own one-pass response from the orchestrator (no R4). ASSUMPTION made explicit: per-task lenses remain principle-valid across artefact transformation; they do not require re-baselining to the post-applier state.'
findings.lens: What unstated assumption is load-bearing in this artefact?
